rationale: D3, data-informed. The laws of D2 on the third-generation droplet forward, revised after a train-only audit of D2. Law changes: radiative extinction comes at one clock unit at the critical diameter and collapses above it (-3.8 per unit of ln(D0/D_crit) instead of -1.2), sooner with helium; the unlit droplet sheds the flame's heat twice as fast in the first two seconds, with an amplitude that grows with its size and a decay time that hardly does; heat-up is slower below 16 % oxygen. Encoder changes: the run's rate offset is trusted far less at 3 and 5 s (only a fifth to a half of it persists on train); the state at the cutoff is read from the end rate of the prefix, so that a droplet that went out one or two seconds before the cutoff is no longer read as burning. Spread: 0.10 before a prefix and 0.06 after, from the train residuals with a margin for unseen sessions; not chosen from validation. Every number typed by the author; no fit, no search.
